A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoRefer Suite. The complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, qualitative results, and a manual evaluation of the dataset reviewer in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and reports additional baseline evaluations in Tables 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The multi-agent data engine, Spatial Token Extractor, Temporal Token Merge procedure, model architecture, and training objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained, including VideoRefer-700K, both VideoRefer-Bench tracks, HC-STVG, Perception-Test, MVBench, VideoMME, and appendix examples. The additional baseline evaluations use existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add LongVU-7B, LongVA-7B, and LLaVA-OV-7B to the existing generalist comparisons. Original comparators remain, and comparator sets for HC-STVG and general video understanding are unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 8 changes the reported Stage 2.5 image-caption training count from 118K to 125K. Appendix B.1 still states 118K, leaving the actual count unresolved and providing no evidence of rerunning training. Evaluation metrics, frame-selection procedures, and other stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The inference-mode, training-data, and token-union ablations in Tables 5-7 are retained unchanged. Appendix reviewer evaluation, qualitative examples, and supplementary visual analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix C.1 retains the same reviewer sampling description, confusion matrix, and summary statistics.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add results for three baselines while retaining existing scores. LLaVA-OV-7B obtains description averages of 2.12/2.48 and question-answering accuracy of 67.4. Its relationship-question score of 64.7 moves VideoRefer's unchanged 59.3 from second to third, behind GPT-4o's 66.0 and LLaVA-OV.

T1.justification: The task formulation, likelihood objective, adjacent-token similarity equation, and reviewer metric definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset, model, and benchmark contributions and the same claims about regional video understanding and general video understanding gains.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations and temporal encoding remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same lack-of-grounding limitation and proposed future extension; the paragraph is relocated rather than newly added.

D1.justification: Figure 8 revises a documented training-data quantity to 125K, creating a discrepancy with Appendix B.1's retained 118K. Other implementation details, training-stage descriptions, hyperparameters, and project/code link targets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for LLaVA-OneVision, LongVU, and LongVA's 'Long context transfer from language to vision' to support the new comparisons. The related-work discussion and substantive research positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Limited wording edits expand the baseline list in Section 4.2.1, and Lidong Bing's affiliation changes to Shanda AI Research Institute. The main narrative, section organization, and appendix explanations remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 expand and reorder baseline rows, with updated ranking emphasis. Several tables and appendix passages move through page reflow, including Table 8 and the limitations paragraph. The existing figure set is retained.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons provide a more informative test of the average-performance claims and reveal a stronger relationship-question competitor, modestly improving the empirical evidence. This benefit is tempered by two reporting inconsistencies: Figure 8 conflicts with Appendix B.1 on the training count, and Section 4.2.1 still claims best or second-best performance despite VideoRefer now ranking third on relationship questions.
